skill.name: x402socks
skill.description: Buy pay-per-use proxy access with USDC on Base using x402, then manage tokens and test regional egress through TLS HTTP CONNECT.
skill.summary: Quote approved proxy purchases, protect access tokens, and verify regional egress with the included shell helper.
skill.author: x402socks

security_audit.summary: Most static matches are Markdown syntax, expected HTTPS requests, local signing, or protected token storage. Confirmed legacy transport paths expose reusable credentials despite explicit opt-in, and malformed credential responses can leak tokens through stdout. No evidence found of prompt injection, unrelated secret harvesting, or intentional malicious exfiltration.

remediation.issue: Opt-in SOCKS5 and plaintext CONNECT expose reusable credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Remove unencrypted authentication paths or require an authenticated encrypted tunnel before enabling them. Keep verified TLS CONNECT as the default.

remediation.issue: Malformed rotation or recovery responses are printed without redaction.
remediation.suggestion: Never print raw credential responses on parsing errors. Emit a fixed error and restrict diagnostic output to explicitly allowed non-secret fields.

content.user_title: Manage x402 Proxy Access and Regional Egress
content.value_statement: Agent workflows may need regional network egress without a recurring proxy subscription. This skill guides approved USDC purchases, token management, and TLS proxy checks.
actual_capabilities: Check service health, list available exit nodes, and retrieve the live package catalog.
Decode live x402 payment challenges and compare quoted amounts against a configured USDC cap.
Provide TypeScript payment examples that filter challenges against independently approved terms before signing.
Save proxy tokens privately, validate access, and inspect account usage.
Rotate or recover access tokens and save replacement credentials with redacted success output.
Test egress IP through TLS HTTP CONNECT and provide curl, Python, Node, and browser client examples.
limitations: Purchases require external wallet signing and funded USDC access on Base; the shell helper does not perform payments.
Service availability, node regions, prices, session limits, and bandwidth entitlements can change.
Legacy SOCKS5 and plaintext CONNECT expose reusable tokens; TLS support is limited to selected exits.
Proxy routing does not guarantee anonymity or permission to bypass restrictions; the Python payment integration requires additional signer wiring.

use_cases.title: Check Regional Application Behavior
use_cases.description: Select a healthy regional exit and verify egress before testing an application you are authorized to access.

use_cases.title: Budget Temporary Agent Access
use_cases.description: Review live packages and approve exact payment terms before provisioning short-lived proxy access for a controlled workflow.

use_cases.title: Restore Paid Proxy Credentials
use_cases.description: Diagnose failed authentication, rotate exposed tokens, or recover settled access using the paying wallet instead of buying again.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Service Availability
prompt_templates.prompt: Check x402socks health and list healthy, enabled exits. Identify TLS CONNECT options. Do not purchase access or display credentials.

prompt_templates.title: Compare a Proxy Quote
prompt_templates.prompt: Quote the cheapest package for a six-hour regional test with a maximum budget of 1 USDC. Present full payment terms and wait for approval.

prompt_templates.title: Verify Existing Access
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my existing private token file to validate access and test a healthy TLS exit. Report the egress IP without displaying credentials.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: verify routing with an existing token.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Guarded Payment Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a TypeScript x402 purchase integration using independently approved network, asset, recipient, domain, and atomic amount limits. Do not execute payment or include secrets.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: review payment controls before deployment.

output_examples.input: Review proxy options before I authorize a purchase.
output: Illustrative review: service health is available and at least one exit supports TLS CONNECT.
The selected package must fit the approved duration, bandwidth, session count, and live payment terms.
No payment has been authorized or submitted.

output_examples.input: A settled purchase returned a provisioning error. Should I purchase again?
output: Do not purchase again when settlement already succeeded.
Retain the settlement transaction hash and prepare a fresh recovery message for the paying wallet.
Submit the ownership signature privately and save the replacement token without displaying it.

output_examples.input: Explain why I should not switch to SOCKS5 after a TLS failure.
output: SOCKS5 does not encrypt the reusable authentication token on the connection to the proxy.
Choose another verified TLS CONNECT exit instead of disabling certificate verification.
Legacy transport opt-in does not remove the credential interception risk.

best_practices: Approve complete payment terms independently and enforce atomic amount limits on the exact challenge selected for signing.
Use verified TLS CONNECT, private token files, and stdin-based credential passing; keep secrets out of transcripts and command arguments.
Check token validity and live node health before retries, and recover settled purchases rather than paying again.
anti_patterns: Automatically sign payment challenges based only on a catalog price or package name.
Enable plaintext proxy authentication, disable TLS certificate checks, or paste reusable tokens into logs.
Repeat settled purchases or use proxy access to evade explicit access restrictions.

faq.question: Which assistant tools are supported?
faq.answer: The skill lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Running its helper requires a client with shell access.

faq.question: What software and funds are required?
faq.answer: The helper uses Bash, curl, and Python 3. Purchases need an x402 client and a wallet funded with USDC on Base.

faq.question: Does the shell helper buy access automatically?
faq.answer: No. It quotes payment challenges and manages credentials. Separate payment examples require explicit authorization and wallet signing.

faq.question: Which proxy transport should I choose?
faq.answer: Prefer verified TLS HTTP CONNECT on port 3129. SOCKS5 and plaintext CONNECT expose reusable credentials and require explicit helper opt-in.

faq.question: Where are tokens stored?
faq.answer: The default token file is ~/.config/x402socks/token. X402SOCKS_TOKEN_FILE or XDG_CONFIG_HOME can change it; the helper writes tokens with mode 0600.

faq.question: What happens if payment settles but the token is lost?
faq.answer: Recover access using the settlement transaction hash and a fresh EIP-191 signature from the paying wallet. Do not buy the same access again.
